key_insight: Contextual Safety Filtering (CSF) adds scene awareness to motion generators, so the same movement can be judged differently depending on what is nearby or who is present. It filters unsafe motions without retraining the generator by grounding safety rules in the current context.
problem_solved: Text-conditioned motion generators can produce motions that are technically correct but unsafe in a specific scene, because they do not understand context-dependent meaning. Existing safety methods rely on prompts, labeled motion data, or fixed geometry rules, and they do not directly model how the surrounding scene changes safety.
method: Uses a training-free filtering stage rather than retraining the motion generator.
Grounds natural-language safety rules in the current scene context to decide whether a generated motion is safe.
Filters motion outputs based on contextual interpretation, not just the action text or generic spatial constraints.
impact: For practitioners, CSF offers a practical way to add safety checks to motion generation systems without expensive reannotation or model retraining. This is especially useful for interactive or real-world applications where the same motion may be safe in one scene and unsafe in another.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing text prompt, scene context, motion generator, and CSF safety filter.

paper_title: CSF: Contextual Safety Filtering for Motion Generators
paper_authors: Lizhi Yang, Yiling Hou, Yao Tang, Junheng Li, Daniel Weng
